# Scaling Secure Identity Service for Millions of K-12 Parents


October 02, 2026


by Shauna Seaver and Nathan Westfall


##


## A Parent Communication App Keeps Families Informed of Bus Service — Even During Severe Weather


For parents of K-12 students, staying up to date on bus changes, ETAs, and pickup/drop-off status helps support peace of mind every day. But when student safety is in question, clear and prompt communication shifts from expected to essential.


When a tornado impacted Deer Creek School District in Oklahoma, a push notification via Tyler Technologies’[My Ride K-12 parent communication app](https://www.tylertech.com/products/student-transportation/my-ride-k-12) quickly notified 1,500 families of suspended bus service. Parents who weren’t users immediately saw the app’s value — the event led to a surge of 4,000 My Ride K-12 enrollments in less than four hours.


## Elastic Scaling Makes My Ride K-12 App Enrollment Seamless for Parents


Without the right infrastructure, Deer Creek SD’s enrollment surge could have caused system slowdowns or crashes. The My Ride K-12 app uses Amazon Web Services to deliver secure, scalable identity and registration services to school districts. These services enable elastic scaling that automatically expands to handle hundreds of thousands of parent registrations on demand and scales back during lower-demand periods, without compromising performance or security policies. For Deer Creek SD’s transportation department, that means significantly fewer parent phone calls about trouble registering or logging in.


“Everything was smooth,” said Transportation Director Robert Feinberg. The transportation department provided simple registration instructions for parents, and the app’s architecture handles the rest. “It was all pretty flawless. Thousands of people were enrolled in less than one day. Within four hours, they were all logged into My Ride K-12 and getting that service,” Feinberg said.


## It was all pretty flawless. Two to three thousand people were enrolled in less than one day. Within four hours, they were all logged into My Ride K-12 and getting that service.


Robert Feinberg


Transportation Director
Deer Creek School District, Oklahoma


## My Ride K-12 Parent App Supports Districts Through Everyday and Unexpected Enrollment Surges


While surges in app enrollment caused by extreme weather are rare, My Ride K-12’s architecture also supports ordinary high-demand periods. The platform currently supports nearly 2 million parents and processes nearly 1 billion notifications annually.


My Ride K-12 enrollment surges happen — and are supported — at a moment’s notice.


At the start of each school year, each district communicates about bus service and the technology available to parents at different times and through different channels. To accommodate this, Tyler’s My Ride K-12 app must be equipped to support the resulting enrollment surges at any time. Whether a district emails 10 or 10,000 parents, app enrollments can come at a moment’s notice.


Back-to-school My Ride K-12 enrollment surges to 2.3 times the average monthly volume.


As districts return to school in August, the app scales to handle activity levels reaching 2.3 times the average monthly volume. In the opening weeks of the 2025-26 school year alone, My Ride K-12 added 359,000 new students, demonstrating the platform’s ability to support school communities at scale. As enrollment grows, scalable functionality enables the My Ride K-12 app to continue supporting school districts — without requiring infrastructure redesigns.


*[Tyler Technologies was recognized as a 2026 AWS Champion](https://www.govtech.com/champions/2026/govtech/tyler-technologies-transportation-division) for our work using AWS to drive digital transformation and better serve their communities. The award highlights Tyler’s use of AWS services to build the identity and registration services powering the My Ride K-12 parent app.*
